haiku-low.q1: It returns the popular-items list with fallback true and version label fallback. No model runs.
haiku-low.q2: It keeps using the stored rows until they are older than 6 hours, then treats them as missing and falls back.
haiku-low.q3: No. Shadow results go only to the prediction log. A shadow failure is logged and counted, and the user's response is unaffected.
haiku-low.q4: Users whose salted hashed user ID falls in buckets 0 to 9 of 100, about 10% of users, always in or always out.
haiku-low.q5: ML lead approval recorded in the registry, at least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, p99 under 80 ms, and a passing feature check.
haiku-low.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided on a live A/B test, and the plan does not assume either option.
haiku-low.q7: Each instance polls the registry every 15 seconds, loads new versions in the background, then swaps its in-memory pointer in one step. No restart.
haiku-low.q8: The request copies the user's feature row into the queued job. A shadow worker runs the candidate later. The request only enqueues and does not wait.
haiku-low.q9: New jobs are dropped and the drop is counted. The user's response is unaffected, and an alert fires if the workers stop.
haiku-low.q10: Each shadow run writes one append-only prediction log record with both models' 20 IDs. A daily job summarizes overlap, error rate, p99, and skip and drop rates.
haiku-low.q11: A feature check runs before loading and whenever an alias moves. A version missing a required feature in the manifest is never run as active or shadow.
haiku-low.q12: One atomic registry write sets active to previous and previous to the rolled-back version. Instances already hold it in memory, so only a pointer changes within a minute.

sonnet.q1: The fallback: the popular-items list with fallback: true and version label 'fallback'. Feature read has a 30 ms timeout; a timed-out or missing row goes to fallback, no model runs.
sonnet.q2: It keeps using the rows already in the store (failed runs never delete rows; retried and team alerted). Readers treat rows older than 6 hours as missing, so it stops using them 6 hours after the last good write, then returns fallback.
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow results go only to the prediction log, never to a response or cache. Shadow jobs are queued after responding, workers run in their own pool, so a slow or crashing candidate cannot hold up an API instance; the user's response is unaffected (even a full queue just drops jobs).
sonnet.q4: A fixed 10% of users: the user ID is hashed with a fixed salt into 1 of 100 buckets; buckets 0-9 are the shadow share. A user is always in or out unless the salt changes. Applies to fallback responses too.
sonnet.q5: It must have at least 7 days in shadow, error rate under 0.5%, and p99 under 80 ms; the ML lead must review and approve it in the registry (recording version, approver, time); and the registry's feature check against the current manifest must pass. An operator then runs the switch action, which is refused without approval.
sonnet.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided whether a live A/B test goes between shadow and the full switch; the plan works either way and doesn't assume it. Any such test would need ML lead approval.
sonnet.q7: Each instance polls the registry at start and every 15 seconds. When an alias points to a version it has not loaded, it downloads and loads it in the background (current version keeps serving), runs the feature check, then swaps its in-memory pointer in one step. No restart or redeploy.
sonnet.q8: The queued job carries the feature row already read in the request (the request asked for features needed by both active and shadow models), so no second lookup. Shadow adds no latency because the job is added to the queue after responding, without waiting on the queue, and workers are a separate pool.
sonnet.q9: The queue has a fixed max size; when full, new jobs are dropped and the drop is counted, with no effect on user responses. If workers stop, the queue fills, drops start, and an alert fires. The daily comparison reports drop rate/coverage of the share.
sonnet.q10: Both go in the append-only prediction log: one record per shadow job with user ID, request time, candidate version, candidate's 20 IDs, inference time, error, skip reason, and the active version's 20 IDs copied from the job. A daily comparison job reads each day's records and writes a summary row per candidate: error rate, p99 inference time, skip and drop rate, and overlap of the candidate's 20 IDs with the active model's 20.
sonnet.q11: A version-level feature check: every feature the version needs must appear in the current feature manifest. It runs before a version is loaded/used (active or shadow) and again whenever an alias moves; the registry refuses a switch if features are missing. Also per-request: active model features missing in the row cause fallback, and the shadow worker logs a skip without running the model.
sonnet.q12: An operator does one atomic registry write setting active back to previous and previous to the version rolled back from. Instances poll every 15 seconds and already hold the previous version in memory, so it is just a pointer swap with no download; target is under 1 minute from the write. Rollback is refused if the feature check fails, and it cannot be written if the registry is unreachable.
